html:
Gwo ka is the drum music and dance of Guadeloupe, played on large barrel drums called ka. It grew among enslaved Africans on the plantations in the 1700s and kept African rhythms alive.

Singers lead call and response songs in Creole, and dancers answer the drums in improvised moves. There are seven basic rhythms, each for a mood or a kind of work. After abolition in 1848 gwo ka was long looked down on as the music of the poor.

From the 1960s it became a symbol of Guadeloupean identity and of the movement for autonomy. In 2014 UNESCO added it to its list of intangible heritage. It is a root of the modern zouk, and it parallels the Haitian and Bahamian drum traditions.
sum: Gwo ka is the drum music and dance of Guadeloupe, played on large barrel drums called ka. It grew among enslaved Africans on the plantations in the 1700s and kept African rhythms alive.
